jobs.title: Lead Civil Engineer, PE - Power & Infrastructure
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Most civil roles are about grading one site after another the way it's been done for decades. This one is different. Yes, you'll design grading, drainage, and foundations and take projects through plan check, but you'll also work shoulder-to-shoulder with our AI engineering team to encode your expertise into a system that produces coordinated site designs faster and more reliably than anything the industry has seen. You won't just be doing the work. You'll be re-imagining how it gets done.

The Opportunity

Monterra is a new kind of consulting engineering firm. We are a team of consulting engineers and technologists specializing in power and energy infrastructure projects (modular data centers, battery storage and microgrids, generators and backup power, and EV charging). At Monterra, licensed PEs direct and supervise our in-house AI agents to deliver faster and better engineering services.

Since launching the service a few months ago, we've been winning and delivering projects, and our client base is growing.

We're hiring our Lead Civil Engineer, our first civil hire. Our projects frequently require both the electrical design that powers them and the civil design that puts them on the ground. You'll own civil across the firm, working directly with our principal electrical engineers to deliver coordinated civil and electrical sets.

Your time will be split across:

  • Client project delivery: civil and light structural design, from grading and drainage to equipment foundations and plan-check responses.

  • Discipline building: develop and continuously improve Monterra's civil engineering standards and processes.

  • AI agent development: liaise with AI engineering team to improve our in-house AI agent.

Our goal is to reimagine how engineering services are delivered and push the frontier of quality, speed, and client experience. As our first civil engineer, you'll be a key part of that journey.

What You'll Do

Site, Grading & Drainage

  • Develop grading and drainage plans for equipment yards, data center pads, and charging lots, including accessible stalls and routes to ADA / CBC 11B.

  • Build existing-ground surfaces in Civil 3D from survey, LiDAR, and aerial site data, and specify topographic and boundary surveys when a desktop surface isn’t enough.

  • Run hydrology and hydraulics, and prepare erosion control and SWPPP plans where the AHJ or site disturbance requires them.

Light to Moderate Structural

  • Design equipment pads and foundations for transformers, switchgear, BESS enclosures, generators, and EV chargers, per ACI 318 and IBC / CBC.

  • Calculate equipment anchorage for seismic and wind per ASCE 7.

  • Know the limits: flag when a structure needs a geotech report or an SE, and scope that work to our sub-consultants.

Coordination & Delivery

  • Coordinate trench routes, utility crossings, and utility pad requirements with the electrical design.

  • Respond to AHJ civil plan-check comments through to permit.

  • Seal civil and structural sheets as the engineer in responsible charge of civil across the firm.

Civil Standards & AI Agent Coaching

  • Set Monterra's civil standards from day one: details library, templates, drawing conventions, and a QC checklist.

  • Document design decisions, rules of thumb, and AHJ-specific requirements to coach our AI agent.

  • Review and QC AI-generated site output, and work with our AI engineering team to improve our AI agent's capabilities.

Who You Are

You're a civil engineer who's always been passionate about your craft but a little frustrated by how slowly the industry moves. You've stamped plenty of drawing sets and worked with clients, and you know what plan checkers look for. But you're also the person who built spreadsheets to automate your own calculations, who thinks about how engineering knowledge could be systematized, and who gets excited about the idea of an AI that amplifies engineers' productivity.

Required

  • Active civil PE license in California, with willingness to obtain comity licensure in other states we work in.

  • 7+ years of site / land development design (grading, drainage, stormwater), including taking projects through plan check to permit.

  • Working structural competence for pads, footings, and anchorage (ACI 318, ASCE 7, IBC / CBC).

  • Fluency in AutoCAD Civil 3D.

  • Strong communication skills: ability to explain engineering rules to teammates outside your field.

  • Qualities we value: intensely curious, strong sense of ownership, self-starter, creative problem solver, and comfortable juggling multiple fast-moving projects.

Preferred But Not Required

  • Structural Engineer (SE) license.

  • Experience on data center, BESS, substation, solar, or EV charging sites.

  • Utility coordination on transformer pads, vaults, and service equipment.

  • Stormwater permitting in CA, AZ, or TX.

  • Experience building automation (e.g., scripts) and using AI tools in day-to-day work.

Compensation & Benefits

  • Competitive salary commensurate with experience.

  • Early-stage equity: you'll be the first civil engineer on a small team, not employee #50.

  • Health, vision, and dental insurance, commuter benefits, unlimited PTO, and more.

  • Remote-first; occasional travel for site visits, conferences, customer meetings, and team gatherings.

About Monterra

Monterra is backed by reputable VC and Angel investors, including Urban Innovation Fund, Base10 Partners, Very Serious Ventures, and more. Learn more about the company here.

jobs.title: Lead MV Electrical Engineer, PE - Power & Infrastructure
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Most power engineering roles are about turning out one-line after one-line the way it's been done for decades. This one is different. Yes, you'll design medium-voltage distribution, run the studies, and take projects through utility review, but you'll also work shoulder-to-shoulder with our AI and software team to encode your expertise into a system that produces coordinated power designs faster and more reliably than anything the industry has seen. You won't just be doing the work. You'll be re-imagining how it gets done.

The Opportunity

Monterra is a new kind of consulting engineering firm specializing in power infrastructure for modular data centers, battery storage, microgrids, onsite generation, and EV charging. Our licensed PEs work with AI agents developed in-house to deliver engineering services faster while remaining in responsible charge of every design.

Since launching the service a few months ago, we've been winning and delivering projects, and our client base is quickly growing.

We're hiring our first MV Electrical Engineer, who will serve as the technical authority and in-house subject matter expert on medium-voltage power systems. You’ll work closely with our Principal Electrical Engineers on projects ranging from modular AI data center deployments and battery storage to heavy-duty truck charging hubs. You’ll own MV technical design, lead the development of our MV engineering standards and processes, and help translate your engineering expertise into the AI-powered workflows that make Monterra different. In this role, your time will be split across:

  • Client project delivery (~60%): full-cycle electrical design, from site layout and one-lines through utility/AHJ review and construction support.

  • Discipline building (~20%): establish and continuously improve Monterra's MV engineering standards, design practices, and quality controls.

  • Shaping the AI (~20%): set the standards and design rules our AI agents follow, and work with our product & engineering team to make them better on every project.

What You'll Do

Substation & Medium-Voltage Design (15-69 kV)

  • Design customer-owned substations and MV distribution for data centers, BESS, microgrids, and large charging sites: develop one-line and three-line diagrams, physical layouts, grounding, and raceway.

  • Specify power transformers, breakers, switchgear, reclosers, and instrument transformers.

  • Integrate generators and BESS at the MV level, including paralleling and transfer schemes.

Studies & Protection

  • Perform short-circuit, load flow, arc flash, and grounding grid studies, and use the results to drive equipment selection.

  • Run the protection coordination study, including relay settings and CT/PT sizing, and develop the MV protection philosophy.

  • Familiarity with substation calculations like system X/R calculation, DC Battery System sizing, surge arrestor sizing, and Harmonic Distortion.

Coordination & Delivery

  • Take MV design packages through utility service and interconnection review.

  • Coordinate equipment pads, duct banks, and site layout with our civil engineer.

  • Respond to utility and AHJ comments and support construction RFIs and submittals.

  • Seal substation and MV sheets on projects where you serve as the engineer in responsible charge.

Engineering Standards & Shaping Our AI Agents

  • Own Monterra's MV engineering standards, including standard details, design templates, and QC checklists.

  • Define the technical rules our AI agents follow, review and validate their engineering output, and work with our AI platform team to continuously improve the system.

Who You Are

You're a power engineer who loves and takes pride in your craft, but also a little frustrated by the monotony and the slow pace of change in the industry. You've designed MV power systems end to end, you know what a utility reviewer looks for, and you can lay out a ring bus lineup any day. But you're also the person on your team who is always trying out and evangelizing new ideas and tools, experimenting with new ways of working, and building spreadsheets or scripts to automate your own studies. If that sounds like you, this could be the right role for you!

Required

  • Active electrical PE license, with willingness to obtain comity licensure in other states we work in.

  • 7+ years of engineering experience, including 5+ years of MV distribution or substation design at 15-69 kV, with ownership of full design packages.

  • Hands-on power system studies in ETAP, SKM, SES CDEGS, PSS SINCAL, or similar.

  • Working knowledge of IEEE substation and protection standards, NEC, and NESC.

  • Proficiency in AutoCAD: you don’t need to be an “AutoCAD wizard”, but should know enough to be dangerous.

  • Strong communication and collaboration skills, including the ability to explain engineering decisions to non-specialists (e.g., software engineer teammates) and work closely with clients and teammates.

  • Qualities we value: intensely curious, strong team player, pursuit of excellence, strong sense of ownership and accountability, self-starter, creative problem solver. Equally comfortable being scrappy or meticulous, depending on the situation.

Preferred But Not Required

  • Experience on high-voltage projects (up to 138 kV class).

  • Experience designing power systems for data centers, BESS, microgrids, solar, or on-site generation, including integration of generators and inverter-based resources into MV systems.

  • Familiarity with protection relays and settings (SEL or similar).

  • Experience with utility service and interconnection requirements across multiple utilities or jurisdictions.

  • Comfort with AI tools and enthusiasm for using AI to improve engineering workflows. No coding experience required.

Compensation & Benefits

  • Competitive salary commensurate with experience.

  • Meaningful early-stage equity: you'll be the first MV engineer on a small team, not employee #50.

  • Benefits including but not limited to: health, vision, and dental insurance, unlimited PTO, and more.

  • Remote-first; occasional travel for site visits, customer meetings, conferences, and team gatherings.

About Monterra

Monterra is backed by reputable VC and Angel investors, including Urban Innovation Fund, Base10 Partners, Very Serious Ventures, and more. Learn more about the company here.
